chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the dog of the Magians: if a Muslim man takes it and names it when he releases it, does he eat from what it catches? He said: Yes, because it is trained (to hunt) and the name of Allah (Exalted and Mighty) is mentioned over it.
ai.seo_question: Is the meat from a Magian's hunting dog halal for Muslims?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the fiqh of using non-Muslim hunting dogs, affirming permissibility based on the principle that the dog is merely an instrument ('mukallab') while the Muslim hunter's invocation of Allah's name validates the catch. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the hunter's intention and verbal declaration rather than the dog's own faith, distinguishing it from other schools that may require the dog to be trained specifically for the Muslim. This ruling underscores the practical application of 'Tayyibat' (pure things) in daily sustenance within the context of interaction with Ahl al-Kitab.
